title: Cached declarative extraction profiles generated by the Model, with bounded browser-agent escalation
summary: Phase A (recommended): the Model Plane generates a declarative ExtractionProfile (selectors plus transforms, never arbitrary code) once per (org, url template, schema, prompt); Quarry validates and caches it per org (not under ZDR) and executes it deterministically on later scrapes, requesting regeneration when validation fails. Phase B (nice to have): during JSON extraction the model can flag that data is behind clicks or pagination and give a goal; Quarry then starts a bounded agent run on the source host, re-extracts the visited pages and merges.
whyItMatters: Phase A cuts per-page model cost for monitors and recurring crawls of the same template, and matches the authority rule: the Model proposes a profile and Quarry executes or rejects it. Phase B covers data hidden behind interaction using both halves Verevon already has (extract and Quarry agent runs).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (engine-and-infra-093 deterministicJson codegen cache; engine-and-infra-092 SmartScrape escalation; api-surface-043)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources in this record set (Firecrawl); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Cache key = hash(cacheVersion, codegen model, url, schema, prompt). Miss: build anchor-context HTML around elements matching schema field hints, a codegen model returns an extractor, run it sandboxed, validate against the schema, store; hit: run the cached extractor and regenerate when validation or selectors fail (10 credits to generate, 3 to reuse). Escalation: wrap the schema as {extractedData, shouldUseSmartscrape, smartscrape_reasoning, smartscrape_prompt}; if flagged start a browser-agent session with the prompt, collect visited pages, re-run extraction and merge.

verevonToday.gap: No extractor codegen, validation loop or profile cache, and no escalation from extract to a browser agent. A declarative ExtractionProfile format (JSON-LD, DOM, AX sources) already exists for agent observations and is the right generation target. The cluster said agent cost budgets are not enforced: agent_loop.rs does charge a flat per-action cost against max_cost_usd, but observation.rs:3164 builds constraints with max_cost_usd None, so whether the Verevon path (Model Plane to Quarry) carries a limit is unverified.

approach: Model Plane: add a profile-generation prompt that outputs an ExtractionProfile validated against the quarry-core schema. Ingestion Plane: validate and execute the profile in quarry-runtime, store it per org keyed by (template URL pattern, schema hash, prompt hash) outside ZDR, and request regeneration on schema-validation failure or selector miss; complete the DOM source of ExtractionProfile if it is partial. For Phase B the Model Plane returns an escalation flag and goal; Quarry starts a bounded agent run (allowed_domains = source host, step and cost budget enforced end to end) and re-extracts.

verevon.exactGap: No model-driven profile generation, validation loop, per-org profile cache or extract-to-agent escalation exists. The existing ExtractionProfile (contracts.rs:259-300) is executed only for agent step observations when the caller supplies it (agent_routes.rs:818-824, observation.rs:646-650), and its executor is a string scanner: DOM and Accessibility fields support only '#id', '[data-testid=...]' or the first bare tag name, values are single strings, NetworkJson and Visual sources are skipped, and there are no list, attribute or transform operations (observation.rs:2261-2355). The item's budget doubt is partly resolved: observation.rs:3164 is test code, but the HTTP step route enforces only max_steps (agent_routes.rs:446-450) and the run TTL; max_cost_usd is accepted at run start and per-step costs are written to receipts, yet no cumulative cost check runs because AgentLoop::over_budget (agent_loop.rs:154-162) is only mentioned in edge comments, never called.

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: a model-authored profile is declarative data that Quarry validates, caches per org and runs deterministically, which fits, but the profile must never contain code and the cache must be per org and absent under ZDR. Quarry calling inference to generate it is currently refused: every Quarry Model Plane feature is OFF by default and model-invoke is granted:false (model_plane_gate.rs:1-14, cross-plane-token-requests.json:40-46), and DEF-QB-T17-PART2 (org-bound, metered path) has no owner. Phase B needs a hard budget end to end, and the gateway starts runs with max_steps 12 and max_runtime_s 120 but no max_cost_usd (browser.rs:483-490).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder and re-source. (1) Make the executor a usable generation target first: back DOM fields with scraper selectors, add multi-valued items, attribute reads and a small closed set of transforms, and version the schema (M to L); the current format cannot express list pages. (2) Wire profile execution into scrape, schedule and monitor paths (a new format or ScrapeOptions field), because today only agent steps run it. (3) Generate the profile on the Model Plane side as a proposed argument when a monitor or source is created, send it to Quarry for validation and storage keyed by (org, URL template, schema hash), and have Quarry return a typed regenerate signal on selector miss or schema-validation failure; this avoids Quarry calling inference while the grant is refused. (4) Phase B only after cumulative max_cost_usd enforcement is added to the HTTP step route (it is absent today).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged at XL, but it now also includes the executor rewrite and missing budget enforcement; do not schedule Phase B before those land.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent is confirmed, but the item is not buildable as described: the profile executor is far too weak to be the generation target, the Quarry to Model Plane inference grant is refused, and Phase B has no cost enforcement on the production step route. Keep Phase A as a later, re-sourced item and mark Phase B blocked.
